acceptance_boundary: Do not hand this correction to family authors as accepted shared infrastructure. findings.title: A child that detaches and is orphaned between observer scans escapes cleanup and can produce false success.
findings.trigger: An actual configured worker spawns a real sleeping subprocess with start_new_session=True and DEVNULL output, writes the correct child_started pid/create_time, emits success, and immediately exits with os._exit(0). This is a genuine child of the worker, not an unrelated-process claim. The process is reparented to PID 1 before the 20ms scanner retains its parent relationship.
findings.actual: run_case returned success twice, with returncode 0, forced=[], survivors=[], errors=[] and no child identity in processes. The reviewer independently inspected the exact child and found it alive with ppid=1 and sid equal to its own pid. Reviewer finally cleanup killed only these exact reviewer-created pid/create_time identities. No source monkeypatch or observer delay was used.

contrast.original_behavior: The rejected helper retained the actual child via the durable event, waited boundedly, terminated it, persisted failure, and did not falsely qualify the worker. Its unsafe reporter-only ownership rule must not be restored.
contrast.normal_exit_behavior: Normal interpreter shutdown happened to leave enough observation time in this run; the child was captured and terminated. This is a spawn/reparent timing gap, not failure for every detached child.

findings.design_requirement: Accepted process_and_resource_contract explicitly includes durable child_started markers for spawn races, natural disappearance of owned descendants as a success condition, and bounded cleanup with durable evidence.
findings.narrow_fix: Retain child hints as evidence candidates without trusting the reporter as signaling authority. Obtain independent pid/create_time and actual session/parent-lineage proof before detachment/reparenting can erase it (for example a small acknowledged registration protocol for controlled workers), or explicitly reject unresolved live child evidence safely. Never manufacture success when a live reported child was not independently classified. Preserve the valid unrelated-process protection and parsing-independent cleanup.
required_regressions: The exact rapid detached child case must fail and the genuinely owned child must be contained once OS ownership is retained.
A live candidate without independently proven ownership must never be signaled on reporter assertion alone or silently treated as evidence of a clean run.
Valid/stale unrelated identities remain alive and outside owned identities; attached/detached natural and stalled children retain behavior.

findings.title: A malformed numeric identity still raises out of event validation before stdout/stderr/result persistence.
findings.trigger: A controlled worker starts a real owned child, writes an otherwise-shaped JSON event whose created value is the integer 10**1000, prints stdout/stderr, and stalls past the three-second timeout.
findings.actual: The corrected helper contains the parent and child, then math.isfinite(event[k]) raises OverflowError("int too large to convert to float"). The parser catches only ValueError/TypeError. run_case raises OverflowError and writes none of result.json, stdout.log, stderr.log; raw events remain. This is a broader existing malformed-event gap in the same durability contract, not a newly introduced numeric calculation regression.
findings.original_behavior: The original helper also leaked both owned processes for this input; reviewer finally recovered only their exact identities. The correction improves containment but leaves durable failure evidence incomplete.
findings.narrow_fix: Normalize or reject oversized numeric identities without allowing OverflowError to escape parser validation. Ensure event validation cannot prevent final result/log persistence after bounded cleanup, recording the specific malformed reason and failing the case.
required_regressions: Oversized created/monotonic numeric values produce durable malformed-event failure, stdout/stderr/result records, and no live owned processes.
Undecodable, unreadable and ordinary malformed event probes remain bounded failures with all raw evidence retained.

original_findings_assessment.P4H-R1: Closed for the specified valid/stale unrelated-PID trigger: independently reproduced original SIGTERM (-15), corrected unrelated sleepers remain alive and absent from owned sets. Actual OS session/parent lineage now controls registration; reporter identity alone does not authorize a signal. A separate detached spawn-race regression remains P4HF-R1.
original_findings_assessment.P4H-R2: Closed for specified undecodable/unreadable file triggers, independently reproduced original owned leaks/no durable evidence then corrected bounded forced cleanup, no live owned processes and stdout/stderr/result persistence. A broader malformed numeric durability gap remains P4HF-R2.
original_findings_assessment.P4H-R3: Closed: identical focused ty independently reproduced 25 original diagnostics and zero corrected diagnostics in both native/eval-installed and optional-absent environments. Runtime shape checks, narrow TypedDict/casts and optional guards replace errors without blanket ignores; owned Ruff import checks pass.

profile_assessment: All 70 real contracts pass with zero skips/errors/failures, including actual child pytest invocations through production profile code for draft/empty rejection, complete frozen Counter equality, duplicate/missing/extra/substituted inventories, strict argv/environment/configured filters and aliases before import, focused labeling, collection-only labeling, setup/call/teardown/collection skip/xfail/xpass/error degradation, original nonzero exits and strict prelaunch spec/worker binding. All 245 preexisting profile contracts also pass. These gates are meaningful but do not exercise the two remaining probes.

collection_assessment.sentinels: Independent real-conftest pre-import finder guards prevent Phase4 family test/worker imports and lazy family optional imports for installed/absent roots, default/dot/tests/base/mandatory/runtime/retained/native/eval scopes; strong full-core guards additionally reject any examples.* imports. Native/eval prerequisites legitimately import their dedicated optional engines. Absent native/eval selected profiles return 4 with concrete missing prerequisite errors rather than success. SSL/Hydra/Lightly-installed state is checked separately because its ANTLR dependency conflicts with llm_eval.
